text:
monica: Quick sync — I opened three smaller PRs for the big docs rename so previews don't time out:
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123 (move files)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4124 (server redirects)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4125 (anchor fixes + internal link updates)

monica: Need recommendations on safe merge order and reviewers. We want minimal broken links on main and keep previews useful for QA.

raj: Thanks. Are the previews up for each PR? Last time the queues made some previews stale for hours.

ci-bot: Preview build queued: docs-preview-784 for PR #4123
ci-bot: Preview build queued: docs-preview-785 for PR #4124
ci-bot: Preview build queued: docs-preview-786 for PR #4125

erin: Looking at a quick run — #4123 preview timed out after 15m on preview-784, logs show dozens of 404s while the site tries to resolve old anchors.

erin: Error excerpt: 
```
ERROR: Broken anchor: /docs/api/old-endpoint#examples not found (referenced from /docs/guides/another-page)
Build status: failed after 920s
```

hannah: My two cents: if anchors are the reason previews die, maybe we land the redirect PR first so old URLs keep resolving during moves. Redirects can map /docs/api/old-endpoint -> /docs/api/new-endpoint and carry anchors through.

raj: Hmm — does our redirect system preserve fragment anchors? I thought cloudfront redirect patterns drop fragments. If the redirect returns 301 to a new URL, the browser keeps the fragment, but our preview server routing sometimes rewrites without anchors. We should confirm.

monica: Good point. I tested locally: plain 301 redirects preserve fragment in browser, but server-side preview routing strips them because it resolves the target doc and then serves it without forwarding the fragment to the static renderer. So redirects alone won't fix anchor resolution in previews.

hannah: Ok then alternate plan: land anchor-fixes first (PR #4125) to ensure internal references point to new anchor IDs, then land move (#4123), finally redirects (#4124) to keep historical links working for external users.

erin: That seems safer for previews but anchor-fixes touch a lot of files — will cause merge conflicts with the move PR. If we do anchors first, you'll need a quick follow-up to rebase move PR.

raj: Tradeoffs either way. Option A: redirects -> move -> anchor-fix minimizes merge conflict but previews still show broken anchors. Option B: anchor-fix -> move -> redirects avoids preview breakage at the cost of extra rebases.

monica: My preference is B (anchor-fix first). QA relies heavily on previews for link checks. We're scheduling a staging deploy at 18:00 PST; if we want the staging to include the rename, we need to be merged before 16:30 to allow preview/build propagation.

hannah: Who's doing the anchor review? I can look at the anchor diffs but need another reviewer for content correctness. @raj can you take verification of API anchors?

raj: Yep, I can. Assign to me for API pages.

monica: Review assignments: 
- anchors (#4125): reviewers @hannah, @raj (priority)
- moves (#4123): reviewer @erin for CI issues and @monica for final structure check
- redirects (#4124): reviewer @hannah and ops for routing validation

erin: I'll also add a CI config tweak in #4123 to increase the preview timeout to 25m for the move run — that should reduce flakiness while previews run re-link checks.

ci-bot: docs-preview-786 for PR #4125 build succeeded (artifact: https://preview.redwood.dev/branches/4125)

erin: Great — anchor PR preview looks green. I spot-checked a handful of pages and anchors link.

monica: OK let's merge #4125 now. After merge, I'll rebase #4123 and trigger its preview.

ci-bot: Merged PR #4125 by monica (commit 7f9a2c)

monica: Rebased #4123 -> pushed. Triggering preview.

ci-bot: docs-preview-789 queued for PR #4123

erin: Preview 789 is running. I'm watching link-check logs. Minor 404s only on a legacy handbook page — will add a fallback redirect in #4124.

hannah: Can we gate redirects so they don't go live until after the move and a canary window? We should avoid immediate mapping public old path -> new path until we've validated anchors on prod. Ops: is that feasible?

raj: Ops confirmed: we can stage redirects in the routing table with a flag `enabled: false` and flip them in a controlled window. Add a short note in #4124 with the staging flag.

monica: Good. Plan recap:
1) #4125 (anchor fixes) — merged (done)
2) #4123 (move files) — rebase + merge after preview green (in-flight)
3) #4124 (redirects) — merge but keep redirects disabled until post-canary flip (ops will toggle)

monica: Merge windows: I'll merge #4123 as soon as preview 789 passes link-checks (target T+30m). We'll do a 2-hour canary after moves before enabling redirects.

ci-bot: docs-preview-789 for PR #4123 build succeeded (artifact: https://preview.redwood.dev/branches/4123)

erin: Green. Link-checker: 0 anchor errors, 3 legacy handbook 404s (fixed in #4124). Ready to merge from my side.

monica: Merging #4123 now.

deploy-bot: PR #4123 merged by monica (sha: c3a21b) — staging preview will update in ~5m

hannah: I'll run a quick crawl after staging updates and report back in this thread. If we see anything major I'll open hotfix PRs.

raj: Thanks everyone. After canary, ops can flip redirects. Leave notes in #4124 about enabling flag and expected flip time.

monica: Thanks all — great coordination. I'll post a follow-up once redirects are toggled. :party_popper:
